The real estate problem

Nobody trained you to be a landlord.

Medre is a healthcare real estate company founded by a commercial real estate broker and a practicing physician. It buys the building a practice needs, leases it to the practice at fair market rent plus a small premium, and writes a purchase option into the documents at year 5 or year 10. It exists for practice owners who want eventual ownership without signing a personal guarantee to get it.

You trained to run a practice. Then the real estate question showed up anyway, and it came with exactly two answers.

Rent, and every check builds your landlord's equity instead of yours. Your renewal terms are their leverage. Ten years in, you own a reputation, a patient base, and none of the ground under any of it.

Or buy, and sign a commercial mortgage with a personal guarantee, produce a six-figure down payment, and become a landlord in your spare time, all while the practice is still proving it can carry the weight.

Both are real options. Neither is a good default. There is a third.

The comparison is the argument

Three ways to hold your space.

Side by side, across the things that actually matter. We shaded the rows we don't win, because you'd find them anyway.

Rent forever Buy it yourself Medre
Capital needed upfront First and last month Down payment, often 10 to 25 percent None from you
Personal guarantee No Almost always yes No
Monthly cost Market rent Mortgage, taxes, maintenance Fair market rent plus a small premium
Who owns the building today Your landlord You and your lender Medre
Path to owning it None Immediate Written option at year 5 or year 10, priced by independent appraisal at that time
If your plans change Walk at lease end Sell or hold a building Renew, relocate, or let the option lapse
Best if You may leave the market You have capital and certainty today You want ownership on your timeline, not your lender's

Buying personally is cheaper over 30 years if you're certain and capitalized. Renting is more flexible if you're not staying. Medre is for everyone in between.

The full mechanics, including the fine print →

Read the fine print first

Here's how we make money.

Two ways. The small premium on your rent, which is the price of your written purchase option. And long-term ownership of good medical buildings when a practice decides not to buy.

That's the whole model. This is not free money and we won't pretend it is. You pay somewhat more than bare market rent, and in exchange your name stays off a mortgage, your savings stay in your practice, and the path to the deed is in writing from day one. Whether that trade is worth it depends on your numbers, which is why the first thing we do on a call is run them.

Is this you

Worth a conversation if.

  • You're opening or buying into a practice and want to plant a flag without betting your house.
  • You're relocating or outgrowing your space.
  • Your lease renewal is coming and your landlord knows you can't easily leave.
  • You already own your building and are weighing a sale-leaseback that doesn't lock you out forever.

Probably not for you if.

  • You have the down payment, the certainty, and the appetite to own today; buy the building, and we'd tell you so on the call.
  • Or you expect to leave your market inside five years; keep renting, stay flexible.
